qt: to the Commission Jessica Polfjärd (PPE) Subject:

Recently, it was officially established that the US has lost its measles-free status after 26 years. Measles, whooping cough and other vaccine-preventable diseases are also spreading in several EU Member States. At the same time, vaccination coverage in some regions has fallen below the level required to maintain a sufficient level of protection for the population. Disinformation and misleading health claims, not least on social media, can undermine trust in vaccinations and science-based information. What is more, low vaccination coverage in one Member State can increase the risk of cross-border transmission. Protection via vaccines is therefore a common European public health issue, despite the fact that responsibility for vaccination programmes is essentially a national matter. With the above in mind: 1.

What practical action has the Commission taken, and what practical action does it intend to take, to counter disinformation about vaccines and other preventive health measures, in particular on social media?
How does the Commission work with the Member States and relevant digital platforms to boost trust in the science on disease and public health?

Does the Commission – in cooperation with the EU’s health authorities and with the support of EU funds – intend to provide further support to Member States in their efforts to increase participation in vaccination programmes?
